examples.en: I saw a huge rhinoceros at the zoo.
A rhinoceros has its horn on top of its nose.
Many wild rhinoceroses live in Africa.
The child drew a rhinoceros and showed it off.

examples.ko: 코뿔소처럼 힘이 센 사람이 되고 싶어요!
examples.en: I want to be strong like a rhinoceros!

examples.ko: 사냥 때문에 코뿔소의 수가 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The number of rhinoceroses has dropped a lot because of hunting.

explain: '코'와 '뿔'이 합쳐진 말로 코 위의 뿔을 그대로 이름에 담았어요. 옛 이름 '무소'도 있지만 일상에서는 '코뿔소'를 훨씬 많이 써요. 발음은 [코뿔쏘]처럼 'ㅅ'이 세게 나요.

phrases.en: The rhinoceros is eating grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주어로 쓸 때 조사 '가'를 붙여요. 동물 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add the subject particle 가 when it is the subject. Common when talking about animals.

phrases.en: The baby rhinoceros is next to its mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아기'를 앞에 붙이면 새끼를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting 아기 in front refers to the young animal.

phrases.en: A rhinoceros's horn is very hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름에 담긴 특징인 뿔을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the horn, the feature built into the name.

explain_en: The word joins 코 (nose) and 뿔 (horn), so the name describes the animal directly. There is also an older word 무소, but 코뿔소 is far more common in daily life. The 소 is pronounced with a tense sound, like [코뿔쏘].

examples.ko: 동물원에서 표범이 나무 위에서 자고 있었어요.
examples.en: At the zoo, a leopard was sleeping up in a tree.
Leopards run really fast.

examples.ko: 표범 무늬 옷은 눈에 확 띄어요.
examples.en: Leopard-print clothes really stand out.
The child found a leopard in the picture book.
At night, the leopard set out to look for food.
I want to run fast like that leopard.

explain: 호랑이는 줄무늬이고 표범은 점무늬예요. 치타는 표범보다 몸이 가늘고 더 빨라요. 옷 무늬를 말할 때 '표범 무늬', '호피 무늬'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I bought a leopard-print skirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 물건의 점무늬를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for spotted patterns on clothes or items.

phrases.en: I saw a black panther in a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 털이 까만 표범을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to a leopard with black fur.

phrases.en: Snow leopards live in high mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 많은 산에 사는 표범이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a leopard that lives in snowy mountains.

explain_en: A 호랑이 (tiger) has stripes, while a 표범 has spots. A 치타 (cheetah) is slimmer and faster than a leopard. For clothing patterns you say 표범 무늬 or 호피 무늬.

examples.ko: 끝없이 펼쳐진 황야를 말을 타고 달렸어요.
examples.en: I rode a horse across the endless wilderness.

examples.ko: 영화는 황야에 홀로 남은 남자의 이야기예요.
examples.en: The movie is about a man left alone in the wilderness.
In the wilderness, I heard nothing but the sound of the wind.
That land was a wasteland a long time ago.
Wastelands often appear in Western movies.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 황야 위에 세워졌다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this city was built on a wasteland.

explain: '들판'은 풀이 있는 평화로운 넓은 땅 느낌이지만, '황야'는 사람이 가꾸지 않아 거칠고 쓸쓸한 땅이에요. 사막처럼 모래만 있는 곳을 말하는 것은 아니에요. 소설, 영화, 노래 가사에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 말을 타고 황야를 달리는 장면이 멋있어요.
phrases.en: The scene of riding a horse across the wilderness is cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 소설에서 넓고 거친 땅을 달리는 장면에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits scenes in films or novels of running across wide, rough land.

phrases.en: The sun set over the endless wilderness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓고 쓸쓸한 풍경을 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress a vast, lonely landscape.

phrases.example: 황야에 홀로 서 있는 나무가 쓸쓸해 보여요.
phrases.en: The tree standing alone in the wilderness looks lonely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼자 있는 쓸쓸한 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a feeling of loneliness.

explain_en: '들판' feels like a wide, peaceful field with grass, but '황야' is rough, lonely land that nobody has tended. It does not mean a sandy desert. You will meet it often in novels, films and song lyrics.

examples.en: They say Jumong founded Goguryeo.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 백 년 전에 건국했어요.
examples.en: That country was founded a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 나라를 건국한 왕의 이야기가 드라마로 나왔어요.
examples.en: A drama came out about the king who founded the country.
People who wanted to found a new country gathered.
Many things happened in the process of founding the country.
It is a country that was founded and has continued until now.

explain: 나라를 처음 세울 때만 쓰고, 회사나 학교를 세울 때는 '설립하다', '세우다'를 써요. 주어는 보통 사람이나 왕이에요. 나라가 주어일 때는 '건국되다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: This country was founded in 1948.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라가 주어일 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the country is the subject.

phrases.en: The king founded a new country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어이고 나라를 목적어로 받는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person is the subject and the country is the object.

phrases.en: We read a founding myth at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라가 세워진 이야기를 말하는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for the legend of how a nation began.

explain_en: It is only for founding a country; for companies or schools, use '설립하다' or '세우다'. The subject is usually a person or a king. When the country is the subject, '건국되다' is more common.

examples.ko: 정부는 경제 난국을 풀기 위해 노력하고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is working hard to resolve the economic crisis.

examples.ko: 회사가 난국에 빠졌지만 모두 힘을 모았어요.
examples.en: The company fell into a crisis, but everyone pulled together.
As the crisis drags on, the employees are getting worn out too.

examples.ko: 지금의 난국은 하루아침에 생긴 게 아니에요.
examples.en: The current crisis didn't appear overnight.

examples.ko: 난국 속에서도 그는 침착함을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even in the crisis, he stayed calm.
The worse the crisis, the more a leader's words matter.

explain: 정치, 경제, 회사처럼 큰 일의 어려운 상황에 써요. 개인의 일에는 '위기'나 '곤경'이 더 자연스러워요. '난국을 타개하다', '난국을 극복하다'처럼 같이 많이 써요.

phrases.en: We joined forces and overcame the crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 상황을 이겨냈다고 할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical pairing for getting through a difficult situation.

phrases.en: The new president broke through the company's crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막힌 상황을 풀어 나간다는 느낌이 있고 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests breaking through a deadlock; fairly formal.

phrases.en: The economy has fallen into a crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 상황에 놓이게 됐을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a situation has become difficult.

explain_en: It is used for difficult situations in big matters like politics, the economy or a company. For personal problems, '위기' or '곤경' sounds more natural. It often pairs with '타개하다' and '극복하다', as in '난국을 타개하다'.

examples.ko: 그동안 숨겨 온 거짓말이 만천하에 드러났어요.
examples.en: The lie that had been hidden all this time was revealed to everyone.

examples.ko: 기자가 이 사실을 만천하에 알리겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: The reporter said he would let the whole world know this fact.
I made a promise in front of the whole world.

examples.ko: 만천하의 눈이 이 재판에 쏠려 있어요.
examples.en: All eyes are on this trial.

examples.ko: 비밀이 만천하에 공개돼 회사가 발칵 뒤집혔어요.
examples.en: The secret was made public, and the company was thrown into an uproar.

examples.ko: 부끄러운 일이 만천하에 알려질까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried that something embarrassing will become known to everyone.

explain: '만천하에 알리다, 드러나다, 공개되다'처럼 쓰고, 숨기던 일이 모든 사람에게 알려진다는 느낌이에요. 보통 조사 '에'와 함께 나오고 뉴스나 연설에서 자주 들려요. 일상에서는 '다 알게 되다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 기자가 이 사실을 만천하에 알리겠다고 했어요.
phrases.en: The reporter said he would let the whole world know this fact.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 모든 사람에게 알린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning to inform everyone.

phrases.en: What had been hidden came out for all to see.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨기던 일이 모두에게 알려졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something hidden becomes known to everyone.

phrases.en: His letter was made public for all to see.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자료나 이야기가 널리 공개될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when documents or stories are made widely public.

explain_en: It is used in phrases like '만천하에 알리다', '드러나다' and '공개되다', carrying the feeling that something hidden becomes known to everyone. It usually comes with the particle '에' and is often heard in news and speeches. In daily talk people say '다 알게 되다'.

en: to be established; to be founded

examples.ko: 이 학교는 백 년 전에 설립됐어요.
examples.en: This school was founded a hundred years ago.
A new company is being established in Seoul.
Once the foundation is established, it will give scholarships.
It's a publishing company founded in 1990.
I covered the process of the institute being established.

examples.ko: 아직 설립되지 않은 단체라서 이름이 없어요.
examples.en: It's an organization not yet established, so it has no name.

explain: 회사, 학교, 단체, 재단처럼 조직을 세워 만드는 일에 써요. 건물을 짓는 것은 '세워지다/지어지다'라서 구분돼요. 회사 소개에서 '○○년에 설립된'이라는 말이 아주 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I work at a company that was founded last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: This foundation was established in 2005.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-되었어요'는 '-됐어요'보다 조금 격식 있게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: -되었어요 sounds slightly more formal than -됐어요.

phrases.en: Do you know the year this school was founded?
phrases.nuance_ko: 세운 해를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for the year something was founded.

explain_en: Used for organizations like companies, schools, groups, and foundations being set up. A building being put up is 세워지다 or 지어지다, so they differ. In company intros, the phrase '○○년에 설립된' appears constantly.

gh: formulated or founded; plans, policies, governments
opened for use; accounts, courses, branches
newly set up; departments, schools, rules

p.n: 신설되다 stresses that something new was set up; 설립되다 is the usual word for founding an organization.

en: to be confined; to be imprisoned

examples.ko: 그는 사기죄로 삼 년 동안 수감됐어요.
examples.en: He was imprisoned for three years for fraud.

examples.ko: 수감된 사람도 가족과 편지를 주고받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even inmates can exchange letters with their families.

examples.ko: 형이 수감되는 날 가족들이 모두 울었어요.
examples.en: The whole family cried on the day my brother was imprisoned.
Before he was imprisoned, he was an ordinary office worker.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 지금 교도소에 수감돼 있어요.
examples.en: He is currently held in prison.

examples.ko: 곧 수감될 거라는 소식을 들었지만 믿을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I heard he would soon be jailed, but I couldn't believe it.

explain: '감옥에 가다'보다 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 가두는 쪽은 '수감하다', 들어가는 쪽은 '수감되다'이고, 보통 '교도소에 수감되다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: He is currently in prison.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 감옥에 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of being in prison right now.

phrases.example: 그는 큰 죄를 지어서 감옥에 갔어요.
phrases.en: He committed a serious crime and went to jail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수감되다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 수감되다 and used in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The inmates exercise at set times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수감된 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who is imprisoned.

explain_en: It is stiffer than '감옥에 가다' and is used in news and legal talk. The side that locks someone up uses '수감하다', the one who goes in uses '수감되다', as in '교도소에 수감되다'.

examples.en: On Memorial Day, events honoring the patriotic martyrs are held.

examples.ko: 순국선열의 희생 덕분에 우리가 자유를 누려요.
examples.en: We enjoy freedom thanks to the sacrifice of the patriotic martyrs.

examples.ko: 학생들이 순국선열 묘역을 찾아 꽃을 놓았어요.
examples.en: The students visited the martyrs' cemetery and laid flowers.
Everyone observed a moment of silence for the patriotic martyrs.
I saw the belongings of the patriotic martyrs in person at the museum.

examples.ko: 순국선열 이야기를 읽고 많은 것을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: I felt a lot after reading the stories of the patriotic martyrs.

explain: 나라를 위해 목숨을 바친 분들을 높여 부르는 말이에요. 현충일이나 기념식 같은 행사와 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, '순국선열께'처럼 높임을 담아 말해요.

phrases.en: We honor the patriotic martyrs on Memorial Day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훌륭한 뜻을 기억하고 높이 받든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means remembering and honoring their noble deeds.

phrases.en: We must not forget the sacrifice of the patriotic martyrs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라를 위해 목숨을 바친 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when speaking of giving one's life for the country.

phrases.en: We observed a silent tribute to the martyrs at the ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: '께'로 높임을 담아 말하는 행사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A ceremony phrase that uses '께' to show respect.
phrases.en_equiv: to give a silent tribute to the martyrs

explain_en: It is a respectful term for people who gave their lives for their country. It often appears around Memorial Day, ceremonies and the news, and is addressed with honorifics, as in '순국선열께'.

examples.en: The company tried to hush up the accident.
It was embarrassing, so the family kept it quiet among themselves.
Hushing up a problem doesn't solve it.
Everyone knew, but the mood was to keep quiet about it.
Even if you hush it up, rumors spread quickly.
Please don't just hush that matter up and move on.

explain: 나쁜 일이나 잘못이 밖으로 알려지지 않게 조용히 덮을 때 써요. 대부분 비판하는 느낌이 있어요. 한 사람이 숨기는 것보다 여러 사람이 입을 닫는 장면에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: You shouldn't hush the problem up and move on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못을 조용히 덮고 그냥 지나간다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a critical tone of quietly covering up a wrong and moving on.
phrases.en_equiv: to hush up and move on

phrases.example: 학교가 쉬쉬하는 분위기라 아무도 말을 안 해요.
phrases.en: The school is in a hush-up mood, so nobody speaks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 입을 닫고 있는 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an atmosphere where many people keep their mouths shut.

phrases.example: 문제를 그냥 덮어 두면 더 커져요.
phrases.en: If you just cover the problem up, it gets bigger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 드러내지 않고 그대로 두는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means leaving a problem as it is without bringing it out.

explain_en: It is used when a bad thing or a mistake is quietly covered up so it doesn't get out. It usually carries a note of criticism. It fits scenes where several people keep their mouths shut better than one person hiding something.

en: to confess; to admit; to make confession

examples.en: The criminal confessed everything at the police station.
If you confess your wrongdoing, your mind feels at ease.
He admitted his lie and apologized.
Some people never confess to the end.
The child confesses to having broken the window.
I didn't have the courage to confess, so I kept hiding it.

explain: '고백하다'는 사랑이나 비밀 같은 마음을 말할 때도 쓰지만, '자백하다'는 자기가 한 나쁜 일이나 죄만 말할 때 써요. 가벼운 잘못에는 '털어놓다'나 '실토하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The police got a confession from the criminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사하는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요. 범죄 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the investigators. Common in crime news.

phrases.example: 그는 모든 잘못을 자백하고 용서를 빌었어요.
phrases.en: He confessed all his wrongs and asked for forgiveness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못을 말한 뒤에 하는 행동을 이어서 말할 때 '자백하고'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 자백하고 links the confession to what the person did afterward.

phrases.en: The criminal never confessed to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝까지 죄를 인정하지 않는 상황을 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for someone who refuses to admit guilt.

explain_en: '고백하다' can be used for love or secrets, but '자백하다' is only for admitting your own wrongdoing or crime. For minor faults, '털어놓다' or '실토하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The soldiers arm themselves heavily with guns and body armor.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 모자와 장갑으로 중무장하고 나가요.
examples.en: On cold days I go out fully bundled up with a hat and gloves.

examples.ko: 중무장한 경비원이 은행 앞에 서 있어요.
examples.en: A heavily armed guard is standing in front of the bank.

examples.ko: 겨울 산에 갈 때는 단단히 중무장해야 해요.
examples.en: When you go up a mountain in winter, you have to gear up properly.

examples.ko: 아이는 우산과 장화로 중무장하고 비 오는 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: The child, fully equipped with an umbrella and rain boots, walked down the rainy road.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 커피와 간식으로 중무장하고 도서관에 가요.
examples.en: During exams I go to the library stocked up with coffee and snacks.

explain: 군대 이야기 말고도 옷이나 장비를 잔뜩 갖추고 나설 때 가볍게 써요. 반대로 간단하게 갖추는 건 '경무장하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I climbed the mountain fully geared up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'으로 뒤의 말을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing what follows.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 우비와 장화로 중무장하고 나갔어요.
phrases.en: It rained a lot, so I went out fully geared up with a raincoat and boots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형 '-고'로 다음 행동과 이어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The connective -고 links it to the next action.

phrases.en: It was a short walk, so I went out lightly equipped.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중무장하다'와 반대로 간단하게 갖출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 중무장하다, for equipping lightly.

explain_en: Besides military talk, it is used lightly when someone sets out with lots of clothes or gear. The opposite, equipping lightly, is '경무장하다'.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 전쟁이 나자 징병을 시작했어요.
examples.en: That country started a draft when the war broke out.
Draft notices arrived for the young men.
Many families were separated because of conscription.

examples.ko: 징병을 피하려고 외국으로 떠난 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: There are people who left for other countries to avoid the draft.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 징병과 모병의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned the difference between conscription and volunteer recruitment.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 징병 연령을 낮추는 문제를 다루고 있어요.
examples.en: The news is covering the issue of lowering the draft age.

explain: '입대'는 군대에 들어가는 사람 쪽에서, '징병'은 나라가 사람을 불러 모으는 쪽에서 하는 말이에요. 반대로 스스로 지원해서 군인을 모으는 건 '모병'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 '군대에 가다'라고 하고, '징병'은 뉴스나 역사 수업에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The country drafted young men.
phrases.nuance_ko: '징병'에 '하다'를 붙여 나라가 사람을 군대에 부른다는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '하다' makes it the action of a state calling people into the military.

phrases.en: Twenty-year-old men are subject to the draft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에 불려 가야 하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the people who must be called to the military.

phrases.en: He went abroad to avoid the draft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에 불려 가는 것을 피한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means avoiding being called into the military.

explain_en: '입대' is said from the viewpoint of the person joining the military, while '징병' is from the viewpoint of the state calling people up. The opposite, recruiting volunteers, is '모병'. In daily talk people say '군대에 가다', and '징병' appears mostly in news and history lessons.
